Subject: Children's ibuprofen recall: it's the syringe, not the medicine

Important for parents: Corvane children's ibuprofen recall

Many of you have seen posts about a children's ibuprofen recall and are worried. I want to explain exactly what is going on and what you need to do.

What is recalled
Corvane Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL (berry), 120 mL bottle
Lot CV6114A and lot CV6114B (exp. 08/2027)
The lot number is printed on the bottom of the box. Please check the box before anything else.

What the problem is
The problem is the plastic dosing syringe that comes in the box. The numbers were printed wrong. Every mark measures DOUBLE what it says:
- the line marked 2.5 mL actually measures 5 mL
- the line marked 5 mL actually measures 10 mL
So a parent who followed the directions exactly with this syringe gave about twice the dose.

The medicine itself is fine. The manufacturer confirmed the liquid meets all specifications. It is not contaminated, it is not expired, and it is not part of the recall. Only the syringe is.

What to do if you have one of these lots at home
1. Throw away the syringe that came in the box. Don't use it for this or any other medicine.
2. Get a correctly marked oral syringe. We have free replacement syringes arriving this morning before noon. Anyone can come in for one. You don't need a receipt and you don't need to have bought it from us.
3. If you'd rather not keep the product, bring it back and we will give you a full refund.
4. Don't use a kitchen spoon to measure.

If your child already had medicine measured with this syringe
I know everyone wants a quick answer, but I can't safely assess a child through Facebook. Whether a double dose is a problem depends on your child's weight, how many doses they had, how close together, and other health things like kidneys. The poison centre can do that assessment properly with you on the phone, and it's free, 24/7.

If you have ANY doubt about how much your child got, call the poison centre: 1-844-POISON-X (1-844-764-7669)

Do not give another dose of ibuprofen until the poison centre or your doctor tells you it's okay.

Call 911 or go to emergency right away if your child:
- is very sleepy or hard to wake up
- is vomiting blood
- is not peeing
- has a seizure

When we found out, and why we didn't call you
We got the recall notice from Corvane on the evening of November 6. We took the remaining bottles off the shelf and put signs on our front door and in the kids aisle the next morning, November 7. This medicine is sold off the shelf, with no prescription. For most of these sales we have no name and no phone number, so we couldn't call people. That's why I'm posting here. Please share this with any parent who might have this medicine at home.

Extra hours for exchanges
We are opening this Saturday 10 am to 4 pm just for syringe exchanges and returns, along with our regular hours.

Our phones are very busy right now. We are returning every call, but if you're worried about your child, please don't wait for us. Call the poison centre first.

Rania Haddad, Pharmacist
Cedarbrook Pharmacy, Erin Mills Pkwy
